s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Lesions are scattered and erythematous
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa are not involved
Laboratory tests showed no abnormal findings
Skin biopsy revealed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and atrophy of the epidermis
Histopathology showed well-developed cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

shortlist.label: Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of pruritic papules with cornoid lamellae on histopathology

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis of Mibelli
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by the presence of cornoid lamellae, which were found in the patient's skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with keratotic papules and histopathological features such as dyskeratosis and suprabasal acantholytic dyskeratosis

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by pruritic papules and histopathological features such as dyskeratosis and acantholysis

shortlist.label: Disseminated superficial porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of multiple, scattered, and pruritic papules with characteristic histopathological features

raw.rationale: The presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae, individual cell dyskeratosis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis, along with the clinical presentation of scattered, erythematous, annular papules, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Porokeratosis of Mibelli
rejected.why: Typically presents with larger, solitary or few lesions, which does not match the scattered, multiple lesions in this case

rejected.label: Darier disease
rejected.why: Characterized by greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and palmoplantar keratoderma, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Grover disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with sudden onset of pruritic papules, often with a history of sun exposure or other triggering factors, and histologically shows suprabasal acantholysis, which is not described here

rejected.label: Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis
rejected.why: While similar, the lack of specific mention of sun-exposed areas being predominantly affected and the presence of atrophy of the epidermis and individual cell dyskeratosis points more towards disseminated superficial porokeratosis
